text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Government vows to curb public deficits to three percent of GDP for 1998, a 15 percent tax rise on corporate profits will be applied to 1997 and 1998.
-- Audit of public finances released on Monday forecasts a public deficit reaching 3.5 to 3.7 percent of GDP if no corrective action is taken, calls for cuts in public spending.
-- France Telecom to buy a 33 percent stake in Senegal's telecommunications operator Sonatel.
-- Engineering group Technip and nuclear materials group Cogema to streamline their chemical engineering activities through a merger of SGN unit Krebs and Technip unit Speichim.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Corporate tax on profits for companies with a turnover above 50 million francs to be raised to 41.6 percent for 1997 and 1998, government expects 22 billion francs from the tax rise.
-- Shares in insurer GAN rose by some 4.3 percent on government's confirmation of a privatisation process.

-- Consumer credit rose by 3.1 percent in 1996, according to national statistics office INSEE, businesses' indebtedness is decreasing and firms are financing investment from their own cash flow, report says.
L'AGEFI
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn launches investigation into status of savings banks Caisses d'Epargne.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Belgian businessman Albert Frere increases stake in Suez -Lyonnaise des Eaux to above 10 percent.
-- Government expected to file with European Commission this week a preliminary plan for Credit Lyonnais privatisation
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault resigns from board of Guinness as a protest against merger plans between Guinness and GrandMet.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French government raises tax on corporate profits in bid to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
